resolved_title: Calderdale Excellence Partnership: IPEELL. Evaluation report and executive summary (EEF, November 2018; lead evaluator Carole Torgerson)
notes: Recoded from the correct document. text/898-torgerson-2018.txt is the EEF IPEELL effectiveness trial (84 schools, Leeds and Lincolnshire; Years 5 and 6, US grades 4 and 5); abstracts/898-torgerson-2018.txt is still the unrelated phonics tertiary review and was ignored. Kraft's four effects and n (0.11 with n 2196 is the two-year writing result in Table 1; 2465 is the one-year trial; -0.17 is the one-year KS2 reading effect on p. 30) match this report's full-sample results, so mixed_samples 0. Kraft's authors Brooks and Higgins do not appear on this report; Torgerson and Gascoine do. Student rule is explicit: whole year groups, parental opt-out only, delivered to the whole year (p. 12 to 13). Confidence medium rather than high because recruitment 'preferentially targeted schools with high proportions of FSM pupils and high proportions of children achieving below age-expected levels at KS2' (p. 12), but the only school eligibility rule was being a Leeds or Lincolnshire primary school not rated Inadequate, and the report presents the schools as near national norms except for FSM (33 versus 14.5 percent). If a reviewer treats the recruitment preference as a selection rule, the alternative is targeted_low, level school.

evidence_quote: We used a joiners model for the student sample, where all students with consent to participate who were enrolled in a randomized teacher’s classroom at the time of post-testing were eligible for inclusion in the analytic sample.
evidence_location: p. 5 (report page numbering, Sample Attrition and Cluster Baseline Equivalence)
resolved_title: Effects of the first year of a three-year CGI teacher professional development program on grades 3-5 student achievement: A multisite cluster-randomized trial (Research Report No. 2018-25)
notes: Full text. Teacher PD trial: 149 volunteer grade 3-5 mathematics teachers in 32 schools and nine Florida districts chosen to represent the regions' diversity, not selected on need (p. 3, Setting and Enrollment). Teachers were randomized within school blocks; all consented students in their classrooms were in the sample, with no achievement or characteristic rule. Teacher volunteering is not selection on need (tie-breaker 6). Parental consent was for data collection in whole classes, not an application, so opt_in is 0. WWC sample text agrees (teachers volunteered; 1,683 students in grades 3-5 with fall and spring scores), and Kraft's n of 1683 matches the analytic sample in Table A1.
